subject: Mathematics
title: Binomial Theorem
summary: For a positive integer n, (x + a)ⁿ = Σ C(n, r) xⁿ⁻ʳ aʳ, with n + 1 terms. The general term Tᵣ₊₁ = C(n, r) xⁿ⁻ʳ aʳ is the key to almost every question.
Typical questions: a specific term or coefficient, the term independent of x, the middle term(s), the greatest coefficient, and sums of binomial coefficients.

Binomial coefficients follow Pascal's triangle; their sum is 2ⁿ, and the sums of alternate coefficients are each 2ⁿ⁻¹. Remainders of large powers are found by writing the base near a multiple of the divisor.

formulas.name: General term
formulas.mistake: It is the (r + 1)th term, not the rth.

formulas.name: Middle term
formulas.formula: n even: one middle term T(n/2 + 1);  n odd: two middle terms T((n + 1)/2) and T((n + 3)/2)

formulas.name: Term independent of x
formulas.formula: set the power of x in Tᵣ₊₁ equal to 0 and solve for r

formulas.name: Sum of coefficients
formulas.formula: put x = 1 (and every other variable 1) in the expansion

formulas.name: Binomial coefficient sums
formulas.formula: C₀ + C₁ + … + Cₙ = 2ⁿ;  C₀ + C₂ + … = C₁ + C₃ + … = 2ⁿ⁻¹;  C₀ − C₁ + C₂ − … = 0

formulas.name: Pascal's rule
formulas.formula: C(n, r) + C(n, r − 1) = C(n + 1, r);  C(n, r) = C(n, n − r)

formulas.name: Hockey-stick identity
formulas.when: Sum of the same coefficient C(k, r) over many powers k — e.g. coefficient of xʳ in (1 + x)ʳ + (1 + x)ʳ⁺¹ + … + (1 + x)ⁿ.
formulas.note: Comes from applying Pascal's rule repeatedly. Terms with k < r contribute 0.

formulas.name: Greatest coefficient
formulas.formula: n even: C(n, n/2);  n odd: C(n, (n − 1)/2) = C(n, (n + 1)/2)

formulas.name: Weighted sum
formulas.when: Sums with r multiplied in (differentiate (1 + x)ⁿ).

formulas.name: Coefficient in Σ k(1 + x)ᵏ
formulas.when: Coefficient of xʳ in (1 + x) + 2(1 + x)² + … + n(1 + x)ⁿ.
formulas.note: Alternative: treat the series as an AGP, sum it in closed form, then read off the coefficient.

formulas.name: Number of terms
formulas.formula: (x + a)ⁿ: n + 1 terms;  (x + y + z)ⁿ: C(n + 2, 2) terms

examples.title: Term independent of x
examples.problem: Find the term independent of x in (x² + 1/x)⁹.

examples.title: Middle term
examples.problem: Find the middle term of (1 + x)¹⁰.

examples.title: Number of terms
examples.problem: How many terms are there in (2x − 3y)¹⁵?

examples.title: Weighted hockey-stick
examples.problem: Coefficient of x² in (1 + x) + 2(1 + x)² + 3(1 + x)³ + 4(1 + x)⁴?
examples.solution: Need Σ k·C(k, 2) for k = 2 to 4. Split k·C(k, 2) = 2C(k, 2) + 3C(k, 3), then hockey-stick: 2C(5, 3) + 3C(5, 4) = 20 + 15 = 35. Check directly: 2·1 + 3·3 + 4·6 = 35.

topics.title: Pascal's triangle
topics.explain: Each entry is the sum of the two above it; row n gives the coefficients of (x + a)ⁿ. The triangle is symmetric because C(n, r) = C(n, n − r).

topics.title: Expansions with negative signs
topics.explain: (x − a)ⁿ = Σ (−1)ʳ C(n, r) xⁿ⁻ʳ aʳ — signs alternate. (x + a)ⁿ + (x − a)ⁿ keeps only odd-numbered terms (even powers of a); the difference keeps the others.

topics.title: Divisibility and remainders
topics.explain: To show 9ⁿ − 8n − 1 is divisible by 64, write 9ⁿ = (1 + 8)ⁿ and expand: the first two terms cancel and the rest contain 8². For remainders, express the base as (multiple of divisor ± 1).

topics.title: Numerically greatest term
topics.explain: Find the term whose ratio Tᵣ₊₁/Tᵣ = ((n − r + 1)/r)|a/x| first drops below 1 — that term is numerically greatest.

topics.title: Coefficient tricks
topics.explain: For the coefficient of xᵏ in a product like (1 + x)ᵐ(1 + x)ⁿ, use C(m + n, k), or multiply general terms and sum over matching powers.

ratta: n + 1 terms;  middle T(n/2 + 1) for even n.
ΣC² = C(2n, n);  Σ rC(n, r) = n2ⁿ⁻¹.
Hockey-stick: C(r, r) + C(r + 1, r) + … + C(n, r) = C(n + 1, r + 1).
